certification.packaging: npm packages installed in node_modules and imported by name (Netlify's documented npm support for Edge Functions; no import map, no npm: specifiers), bundled by the CLI's edge-functions bundling step during the --no-build deploy. The two Wasm modules and the font are static files in the publish directory, fetched as bytes from the request origin on first render and passed to createEdgeOg as resvg.wasm and layout.wasm, so neither Wasm module is inside the edge bundle.

bundle.note: Measured from the local bundle the CLI produced for this deploy. It is smaller than the first certification's 3292842-byte bundle because createEdgeOg now imports only satori/standalone.

certification.cpuLimit: Netlify documents 50 ms of CPU per request (https://docs.netlify.com/build/edge-functions/limits/); every observed render, including the first requests after each deploy, returned 200, so the limit did not block them. CPU time per request was not measured

caveat.observed: 2026-11-01, deploy 6ae7a0b5dd9e780c65a1acf3 (the edge site's first deploy, same fixture sources)
caveat.symptom: /og-edge/hosted and /og-edge/edge returned 200 image/png 1200x630, but both were the same solid #064e3b card with no text: identical ETag (062b3cea...c478) and image entropy 0.000. verify-url's format, dimension, and content-type checks alone would have accepted them. The CDN cached both for 24h under Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400, so those slugs are not used as evidence.
caveat.cause: Fixture layout, not the runtime. The card was width 100% and height 100% with padding 64 and alignItems flex-end. Satori sizes boxes as content-box, so the card was 1328x758 and its content ended at y=694 on a 630px canvas. A title that fits on one line ("hosted · metaplate/edge on Netlify Edge", "edge · ...") was drawn entirely below the canvas, leaving the solid background. Longer titles wrap to two lines and the upper line lands on the canvas, which is why cert-990d8a and cert-d16553 rendered text. Reproduced locally on demand with satori 0.63.2, @resvg/resvg-js 2.6.2, and the fixture's exact style: hosted and edge render a 4418-byte single-colour PNG, while cert-990d8a and cert-d16553 render 19767 and 19452 bytes, matching the certified responses byte for byte.
caveat.withdrawnDiagnosis: The original record attributed the blank cards to a first-deploy propagation race on the same-origin font fetch. That was wrong: every asset fetch returned the right bytes because nothing was failing, and the cold-start slugs that rendered text were long enough to wrap.
caveat.resolution: The fixture now sets boxSizing: "border-box" (commit c5d9f005703cf1ba1e14c96ebeede0446950df54). Deploy 6ae7ee5478780e9836d6fa03 serves it; the one-line titles e1 and bx-short render text, verified below. The decoded-content check stays on every hosted certification.

routes.evidence: .planning/hosted-evidence/cloudflare-workers-2026-11-01.json; fixture examples/hosted/cloudflare/worker; local wrangler dev --local (workerd) reproduction, no Cloudflare deployment
routes.reason: Every render fails on Workers. A Worker built from the packed 0.8.0 tarball (resvg.wasm and layout.wasm imported as WebAssembly.Module values, Wrangler 4.156.0 dry-run bundle 4551 KiB / 1636 KiB gzip) returned 500 for every request under wrangler dev --local (workerd) on 2026-11-01. Satori's bundled HarfBuzz Emscripten glue sees WorkerGlobalScope and reads self.location.href, which Workers do not define: "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'href')". With globalThis.location defined as a probe, it then compiles HarfBuzz from embedded bytes, which Workers forbid: "RuntimeError: Aborted(CompileError: WebAssembly.instantiate(): Wasm code generation disallowed by embedder)". Satori accepts no precompiled HarfBuzz module, and every Satori release that exports satori/layout.wasm (0.35.2 and later) bundles this glue, so no caller-side fix exists; metaplate/edge rethrows either failure as an error naming the limitation.
routes.runtimeBoundary: Local workerd through wrangler dev --local only; nothing was deployed to a Cloudflare account. Deno-based edges (netlify-edge) allow run-time Wasm compilation and are unaffected.
